plates.side_label: 1736–1928 TIMELINE · BELCHIER & DUHAMEL MADDER RINGS, KÖLLIKER OSTEOCLASTS, CULMANN-WOLFF CRANE LAW & CHICK-MCCOLLUM VITAMIN D
plates.quality_reason: Flow-first: a teach diagram, chart, counter or timeline is a £0 code graphic. No Flow mint.
plates.reference: Own code graphic: on period paper, the 3-era timeline completes: 1736–1739 & 1873 (John Belchier and Duhamel du Monceau use red madder-root dye to prove bones grow in living rings, and Albert von Kölliker discovers bone-dissolving osteoclasts partnering with osteoblasts) · 1866 & 1892 (Swiss crane engineer Karl Culmann spots principal-stress trajectories in the human femur, inspiring Julius Wolff's Law of mechanical bone remodelling) · 1919–1928 (Edward Mellanby, Elmer McCollum, and Harriette Chick prove in London, Baltimore, and Vienna that Vitamin D from cod-liver oil or ultraviolet sunlight mineralizes bone and cures rickets).

teach_overlay.detail: Animated timeline (1736 → 1928) alongside an inked summary of 10-year osteoblast/osteoclast bone turnover, Culmann-Wolff mechanical stress trajectories, and Vitamin D mineralization
teach_overlay.scale: from crimson pig bones on a London dinner table to an iron crane in Zurich and sunny hospital balconies in Vienna, scientists discovered how your body rebuilds its entire skeleton every ten years
